subject: Aurora Health — marketplace bundle anchoring & reseller passback path
messages:
From: Liam Park <liam.park@aurorahealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aurorahealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Health RFP: marketplace bundle anchoring and channel passback

Hi Grace,

Thanks for speaking with our team last week. We ran into a few follow-ups on the RFP scope (attached). Two items we'd like clarity on before we proceed to internal approval:

1) Bundle anchoring: Aurora is looking to list a multi-feature bundle on Azure Marketplace that contains hosted inference and a managed private option. We need to understand how Redwood intends to anchor list price vs. private-offer price so our procurement system can validate the bundle against our price controls.

2) Reseller passback path: our channel team requires a clear mapping of how any private-offer discounts will be split/credited to our reseller partner (HealthTech Distributors) and how Redwood will report net revenue for invoicing. Specifically: timing of passback, evidence we must submit, and whether Redwood can honor a channel uplift.

We've attached the RFP and a sample pro forma. Can your team propose a passback/options matrix (preferred, acceptable, fallback) and an anchored pricing example for the bundle (list price, committed private-offer price, and suggested reseller uplift %)?

Best,

Liam Park
Sourcing Manager — Aurora Health
liam.park@aurorahealth.com

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Liam Park <liam.park@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora Health RFP: marketplace bundle anchoring and channel passback

Hi Liam —

Thanks for sending the RFP and pro forma. Appreciate the level of detail. Short answers first: yes, we can do an anchored bundle listing with a separate private-offer price, and yes, we support a reseller passback workflow with documented evidence for invoicing.

I've looped in Ben (channel ops) and Irene (marketplace & legal) to propose a concise matrix. We'll aim to send a short proposal by EOD Wednesday. Would Aurora be OK with a call on Thursday to walk through the matrix and check any procurement validation fields?

High level notes before the call:
- List price vs private-offer: we typically suggest listing the bundle at a higher published list price and then provide a private-offer discount that maps to your committed term. This preserves marketplace visibility while keeping private offer accounting separate.
- Reseller uplift: common patterns are 5–15% uplift depending on whether the reseller will manage billing or simply receive a commission credit. For managed billing where the reseller invoices Aurora directly, we usually use a passback evidence file and timing tied to the invoice period.
- Evidence: we can accept either (a) reseller invoice referencing private-offer id + signed SOW, or (b) HubSpot deal export + reseller acceptance email.

Will send the matrix + a sample anchored price table shortly.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Head of Deal Strategy, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Liam Park <liam.park@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aurora Health RFP: marketplace bundle anchoring and channel passback

Hi Liam / Grace,

Attached is a compact passback matrix and proforma (redwood-proforma-bundle-v1.xlsx). I built three options: Preferred (managed billing + 8% reseller uplift), Acceptable (Redwood invoices Aurora, reseller receives 6% commission via quarterly credit), and Fallback (no uplift; reseller is handled outside marketplace). Key bullets:

- Preferred:
  * List price: $115k/yr
  * Private-offer committed price: $90k/yr (22% off list)
  * Reseller uplift: 8% of net (applied as a credit to reseller on payment schedule)
  * Passback timing: quarterly, supported by reseller monthly invoice + private-offer ID

- Acceptable:
  * List price: $115k/yr
  * Private-offer price: $92k/yr (20% off list)
  * Reseller commission: 6% paid as rebate to reseller after proof of delivery
  * Passback timing: quarterly, Redwood issues credit memo to reseller ledger

- Fallback: minimal discounting allowed on marketplace listing; reseller handled by Aurora outside of marketplace flows.

Notes on evidence: reseller invoice must reference the private-offer ID and the Aurora purchase order. Our marketplace tooling will produce a reconciliation CSV that Aurora can use for accounting reconciliation.

Open Qs we should confirm on the call: whether Aurora requires the reseller to be invoiced directly (managed billing) or if Redwood can invoice Aurora and route credit to reseller. Managed billing increases complexity (KYC for reseller, separate tax handling).

-ben

Ben Carter
Director, Channel Operations — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-proforma-bundle-v1.xlsx (xlsx stub)

From: irene_choi@redwood.com <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Liam Park <liam.park@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aurora Health RFP: marketplace bundle anchoring and channel passback

Liam —

Following our internal review, a few legal/accounting clarifications to confirm before we lock terms:

1) Tax handling under managed billing: if HealthTech Distributors will invoice Aurora directly, we need reseller's W-9 (or local tax doc) and confirmation on VAT treatment where applicable.
2) Termination and true-up: private-offer price is honored for the committed term; overages will be reconciled monthly and credited back to reseller net of uplift. We will add a clause to the private-offer SOW to capture overage true-ups and audit evidence.

If Aurora is comfortable with Preferred path (managed billing + 8% uplift), we can prepare a draft private-offer and SOW and route to your procurement for signatures. Otherwise, the Acceptable path (Redwood invoices Aurora) avoids reseller KYC and taxes on Redwood side but means reseller gets a rebate rather than direct invoice credit.

We can keep the call to Thursday to finalize which path you prefer.

Regards,

Irene Choi
Marketplace & Compliance Counsel — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
